properties.description:

for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Wind direction,
magnitude, and timing with these systems will be monitored closely as
a combination of high tide and winds in an onshore direction
could lead to tides exceeding astronomical high tide by a foot or
more.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 4:09PM CST by NWS Grand Forks ND
properties.description:
Light snow across portions of eastern North Dakota and west-
central into northwest Minnesota has led to slippery roads.
While snowfall totals will be less than an inch, this may still
bring enough to impact travel conditions. Snow is forecast to end
by 9 PM, although may linger in far southeast North Dakota into
west-central Minnesota through tonight. Motorists should slow
down to a safe speed and plan extra time for the afternoon and evening
commute. Don't use cruise control. Be especially careful around
stop lights, school bus stops, and intersections.

Check road conditions...
By Phone: call 511
Website for North Dakota: travel.dot.nd.gov
Website for Minnesota: 511mn.org

properties.areaDesc: Hudson; Eastern Bergen; Eastern Essex; Eastern Union
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:57PM EST until November 27 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Hudson, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex and Eastern
Union Counties.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high
tides.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread minor to moderate flooding
of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline,
including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and
businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road
closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will
also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and
bays, including the tidal portions of the Hackensack River and
Passaic Rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if
slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:57PM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM
PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back
in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a
sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday.
Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10
feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by
Friday morning's high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:42PM PST until November 25 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding
with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW)
at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. The alignment of high surf and high tide will
increase the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 1:42PM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large
breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM
PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW)
at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 4:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to hold near a crest through Wednesday before beginning
a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week and
into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM EST Tuesday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 11.9 feet Tuesday,
December 01.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 1:27PM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.0 and 10.4 feet above MLLW at the North
Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may worsen
coastal flooding along exposed beaches.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Thursday morning
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King
Salmon and the Arcata bottoms and sections of Highway 101.
Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous surf conditions and
localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:24PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 121 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue
11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 5:23PM AST until November 25 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S.
Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St.
Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; South Washington Coast
properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 24 at 1:23PM PST until November 26 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible.

* WHERE...In Oregon, Clatsop County Coast and Tillamook County Coast.
In Washington, South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

Consider sleeping in a location that is furthest away from large
trees and power lines. Be aware of your surroundings and where you
are relative to nearby trees and powerlines.

Prepare for potential power outages. If you have a gas-powered
generator, ensure you have enough fuel. Ensure you have batteries,
flashlights, and a way to maintain a safe body temperature if you
were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Storm force winds 40 to 50 kt with gusts 55 to 65 kt.
Very high and very steep wind driven seas will become chaotic
23 to 28 ft at 13 seconds. Winds ease this evening, but a
heavy long period swell builds in and seas remain very steep
and hazardous 19 to 24 ft at 17 seconds.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Storm Warning, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.
For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 4:14PM EST until November 27 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation
above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Wednesday to
10 AM EST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM
Wednesday to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The higher of the high tide cycles will be
during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to
bring minor impacts on Wednesday. The worst impacts are
currently forecast on Thursday. As winds switch to a SW
direction Thursday afternoon minor water level rises (around 1-2
ft) on soundside locations.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most severe and impactful high tide
will be with Thursday morning's high tide, where major tidal
flooding is possible. Further minor to moderate tidal flooding

flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.

officials.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 10:36AM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Highest
surf and impacts likely across west facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Wednesday to
9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, Thursday
morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and
Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.0-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal
Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and
High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of
the respective warnings if they are issued.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 8:31AM HST until November 25 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...
...COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT IN EFFECT FOR ALL HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

.A large, long-period north-northwest swell will build down the
island chain today. While the source low aimed its peak swell
energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at Hawaii to see
surf build to warning levels during the day before subsiding on
Wednesday. An even larger north-northwest swell is likely
Wednesday night into Thursday. Higher than predicted water levels
could lead to flooding of beaches that typically remain dry,
particularly during the pre-dawn high tides Wednesday and Thursday
mornings.

* WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores,
15 to 20 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores. A combination of surf and high water
levels could produce nuisance coastal flooding.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.


* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 6 AM HST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, from 6 PM HST this evening
through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous. Flooding of beaches that are
normally dry, minor coastal erosion, and saltwater inundation.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 12:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid week, remaining steady around
4.3 to 4.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM EST Tuesday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet
early Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Nassau; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Coastal Glynn; Coastal Camden
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 12:00PM EST until November 26 at 4:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 8 feet. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to
3 AM EST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 1 AM to
7 PM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level
is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal
areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 2.5 to
3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to
3.5 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST
Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4
PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second
Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through
Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow
levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high

River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek.

expected in the surf zone.

Counties.

or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday Nov 30.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 110 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
